title: FRONTIER
program: A research program of Ostrium Labs
question: Does deciding which attempt runs next get more independently verified results out of a fixed compute budget?
summary: A deterministic Rust control plane that runs research attempts under a fixed compute budget and accepts a result only through a verifier receipt. Allocation policies — round-robin, Thompson sampling with and without hints, greedy priors — compete for the same budget; every campaign is logged to a hash-chained event log and can be replayed bit for bit.
architecture: frontier-core — specs, attempt DAG, budget ledger, evidence store, hash-chained event log, a portable RNG and libm
frontier-sim — environment, runner, audit; frontier-cli on top
Python layer — property-test verifier, a deterministic task DSL worker, bootstrap analysis, a Docker sandbox
maturity: Simulation and deterministic-task pilots complete; no model-backed study has run

experiments.title: Posterior allocation in simulation
experiments.hypothesis: With heterogeneous success rates, Thompson sampling with hints solves more problems than round-robin at the same budget.
experiments.setup: Simulated verifier, 50 problems, six regime × budget cells, 200 seeds each; 24,000 runs. Paired bootstrap, 95% intervals.
experiments.result: Five of six cells favour Thompson (R5-scarce +12.95). One does not: R2-moderate −0.19. The preregistered rule required every cell.
experiments.limitations: Simulated verifier. The headline values reproduce only with the Windows build's platform libm; later errata re-ran it with a portable libm and no frozen verdict changed.

experiments.title: Why it lost: misleading hints, correlation, verifier noise
experiments.hypothesis: Mechanism M — misleading hints — explains the R2 loss.
experiments.setup: 40,200 simulated runs varying hint quality, problem correlation and verifier false-positive rate.
experiments.measurement: Δ problems verified; share of accepted results that are false
experiments.result: The loss replicates (−0.26). Mechanism M is refuted, though confounded. At a 2% verifier false-positive rate, 8–27% of accepted results are false depending on regime.
experiments.limitations: Mixed scorecard; the mechanism test is confounded with hint optimism, which exp-002 isolates.

experiments.title: Optimistic hints on dead problems
experiments.hypothesis: Mechanism O: optimistic hints send attempts to problems that cannot be solved.
experiments.setup: 12,600 simulated runs sweeping hint optimism λ from 0 to 1.
experiments.measurement: Extra attempts spent on dead problems; Δ problems verified as λ varies
experiments.result: Thompson spends 46.9 more attempts on dead problems; the difference moves from −0.26 to +0.56 as λ goes 0 → 1.
experiments.limitations: Simulation only; identifies a mechanism, not a real-task effect.

experiments.title: First real-task pilot
experiments.hypothesis: Adaptive allocation solves more real (non-LLM) tasks than round-robin.
experiments.setup: 34 deterministic DSL tasks (26 live), catalog order, 2,100 campaigns at budgets 60 / 240 / 480.
experiments.result: +1.02 / +0.62 / +0.28. Reported as supported, then withdrawn: tasks ran in catalog order, which leaks into every policy.

experiments.title: Real tasks, order shuffled
experiments.hypothesis: The exp-003 effect survives when task order is shuffled per seed.
experiments.setup: Same task set, order shuffled per seed, 100 seeds per budget.
experiments.result: Positive at budget 60 (+1.86); not distinguishable from zero at 240 (+0.19, interval crosses 0); hint-free Thompson −0.12. FIFO order alone moves results by −9.03.
experiments.limitations: Effect only at the smallest budget; the hint carries most of it.

experiments.title: How weak is the verifier?
experiments.hypothesis: The frozen acceptance rule separates suites by false-acceptance rate.
experiments.setup: Offline study: 491 known-wrong programs run against each candidate test suite.
experiments.result: The 40-case ±20 suite accepts 1.83% (9 programs); every other suite accepts none — a floor effect, so the frozen rule cannot be tested here.
experiments.limitations: Floor effect: the comparison has no resolution.

experiments.title: The price of a strong verifier
experiments.hypothesis: A stronger verifier suite removes false solves without costing yield.
experiments.setup: v2 suite with 199 checks (0.995 CU per check against 0.215), 2,100 runs.
experiments.baseline: The weaker suite, under each policy
experiments.result: Zero false solves in 2,100 runs — and fewer true solves: round-robin loses 3.93 / 1.88 / 1.06 by budget. Hinted Thompson still leads round-robin by +3.41 at budget 60.
experiments.limitations: Costs are modelled compute units, not measured time.

experiments.title: Tasks with dependencies
experiments.hypothesis: Adaptive allocation helps more when problems depend on each other.
experiments.setup: Catalog v3: 24 dependency problems (19 live), 1,800 campaigns.
experiments.result: +4.44 at budget 120 and +4.45 at 480, shrinking to +0.48 at 1,920. A greedy prior loses 1.92 at the largest budget.
experiments.limitations: A pilot on a constructed task family; not a sealed benchmark.

experiments.title: Fail-fast charging
experiments.hypothesis: Charging a failed verification only up to its first failing case recovers the yield the strong suite cost.
experiments.setup: 3,900 campaigns under a fail-fast charge model.
experiments.measurement: Share of lost yield recovered; Δ true solves
experiments.result: Round-robin recovers 71% / 93% / 96% of the lost yield; dependency tasks +5.07 at budget 120. All six registered checks pass — in the charge model.
experiments.limitations: The saving is modelled. exp-009 tests whether it is physical.

experiments.title: Is the modelled saving real?
experiments.hypothesis: Fail-fast verification saves wall time in proportion to the modelled charge.
experiments.setup: 1,257 candidates × 2 modes × 3 repetitions, timed; four campaigns of 700.
experiments.result: 6.4% measured against 92.9% modelled. About 92% of a verification's cost is fixed interpreter overhead (≈120.5 ms + 0.05 ms per case). Verdicts were identical.
experiments.limitations: One host (i5-1135G7, 8 threads); campaign-level timing was confounded by host load and is reported as uninformative.

experiments.title: First model-backed study
experiments.hypothesis: H1 holds with language-model workers behind the sandbox on a held-out suite.
experiments.setup: Phase 0 only: replay infrastructure tested against a fake transport.
experiments.result: Not run. No provider call has been made; it needs a model, a provider and a spending cap.

experiments.title: Hybrid latent/text reasoning (HybridAgent)
experiments.hypothesis: Hybrid latent/text reasoning changes verified yield per unit of compute.
experiments.setup: Adapter exists; its generate() reports unavailable when it cannot run.
experiments.baseline: A matched text-only model (not yet built)
experiments.result: Not run and blocked: needs the 8B checkpoint reproduced and a GPU training budget. Both candidate comparisons are confounded as designed.
experiments.limitations: Nothing about HybridAgent has been validated.

next: Re-run the allocation comparisons under the measured cost model (fixed overhead + per-case cost)
Stage 2 — the first model-backed study, once a provider, model and spending cap are chosen
